I merged them into w2/W2-160 as 9c507d513, and `gov accept` shows every one red. TESTS-READY names the merge commit. The tests worktree and its branch are removed.

evidence: First line of `gov links --since b42bcff9e`: "gov links: 0 new since b42bcff9e, 1709 standing (UNMARKED_CHANGE orchestrator 10, … commits 2)". `gov accept W2-160` exits 3 with outcome fail, error_kind null, 0 passed, 66 failed, 0 skipped. Per KPI line: success-1 21, success-2 9, success-3 25, success-4 11, failure-1, failure-2 and failure-3 3 each.
tests: 66 collected, 66 red. The test designer gave three reasons for the red: `invalid choice: 'wait'`, `invalid choice: 'helper-watch'`, and the source-search targets not built yet. It saw no collection or fixture errors. Against a throwaway model of I1 and I2 that it built in its TMPDIR, all 66 passed, and each of 12 deliberate faults planted in that model was caught by its intended test.
discoveries: `gov context DAEO-fd0p --role independent-test-designer` refused with CONTEXT_OVER_CEILING (9298 tokens against 6000). I built the packet with `--budget 12000` instead; this is the refusal INVESTIGATION-1 A1-7 describes. Also: `gov launch` writes no `<base>.pid`, as the ticket's fact note already says, so the tests plant the pid files.
risks: S4's filesystem check is strict. During a helper-watch pass it accepts only new or changed inbox items, `helper-watch-state.json` and `helper-watch.log`, so a lock file of the kind W2-159 uses (`.state.lock`) would fail it. The engineer's brief must say so. One S3 test assumes an item carries the last entry's `type` or `timestamp`, which is the test designer's reading of I2's "last line". `git branch -d` printed "could not lock config file …/.git/config" (the sandbox), so a stale `[branch "w2/W2-160-tests"]` section may remain in the main repository's config. The branch itself was deleted.
lessons: `git worktree remove` also deleted the tests tree's ignored scratch, which held the worker's log, summary and tripwire file (`td-1.*`). I had already read and recorded the return and the tripwire before removing it, but next time copy `log/` into the lead's records first.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: The test designer left these open, so no test asserts them: whether "stale" and the 24-hour window read the entry's timestamp or the file's mtime (the tests keep both in agreement); whether `--once` prints the "ended" line; whether workers are still checked when there is no `session.txt`; whether `gov wait` prints `num_turns`; a `<max-s>` of 0 or below; a pid file holding no number.
recommended_next_action: Start the build run. Build the engineer's brief with `gov context DAEO-fd0p --role engineer --budget 12000`, include the S4 lock-file note and copies of the reference scripts `wait_for.sh` and `helper_watch.py`, and launch the engineer on claude-sonnet-5-5, high, `--class C2`.
